source.title: Coding agents are leaking secrets through “Don’t Ask Again”

complete_compiler_story.summary: Apiiro reports finding 2,539 real secrets across 1,994 public repositories after coding-agent approvals stored exact commands in local project settings. In 1,122 of 104,185 public Claude settings files, its scanners found a real secret. The company says automatic ignore rules help only when the file was created normally and never force-added.

Replace broad permanent approvals with narrow command patterns, then test repository checks against an intentionally harmless sample secret.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Google’s Policy-Based Enforcement beta can automatically apply client-side encryption to files matching admin rules across My Drive and shared drives. Encryption happens in place, preserving file URLs, and covers Workspace, Office, PDF, and image formats. The beta also adds user notices, audit records, and alerts when an external key service is unavailable.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Eligible teams should test one narrowly scoped rule against nonproduction files, confirm key-service failure alerts, and inspect user notices and audit logs. The beta requires Assured Controls licensing and allowlisting, so availability and operational recovery need verification before broader rollout.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Reserve Bank of Australia economist Sarah Hunter says AI adoption is fast but aggregate productivity effects remain difficult to measure. She cites a survey where 35% of adopters reported no productivity gain, while 8% were reducing headcount and 6% increasing it. The speech presents estimates ranging from 0.1 to 2 percentage points.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Build an adoption case around measured task time, quality, training, and redesign costs instead of a single economy-wide forecast. Track employment changes separately from productivity, and revisit the baseline as comparable observations accumulate.

source.title: The benchmark where AIs have to lie to win
source.scope: Reviewed the complete benchmark account, game roles, 386-game sample, scoring claims, observed strategies and stated limitations.
source.freshness_reason: This accepted specific-event benchmark remains within the extended 168-hour window; the newer Anthropic memory item was an exact prior-edition duplicate and was rejected.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete benchmark account, game roles, 386-game sample, scoring claims, observed strategies and stated limitations.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Dwarkesh Patel describes Clocktower, an author-designed social-deduction benchmark played across 386 games using roughly $20,000 in API credits. Its roles require cooperation, conflicting private information, and sometimes deception. Reported Elo gaps and win rates measure performance inside this game setup; they do not establish general workplace reliability or deception risk.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Use adversarial role-play as one bounded stress test, then inspect transcripts for coordination failures, unsupported claims, and recovery behavior. Keep the game score separate from real-task evidence and require human approval for consequential actions.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed the full benchmark script, rules, sample size, reported results, strategies and limitations.

complete_compiler_story.headline: A file-safe editing Skill puts recovery before replacement

source.title: AID-2026-0155: Claude Code deletes 15 years of Harvard law professor’s course materials
source.scope: Reviewed the incident chronology, original-post references, deletion scope, Dropbox recovery and database warning that the record remains draft and unverified.
source.freshness_reason: The accepted specific event falls inside 168 hours; the source is explicitly labeled draft and unverified, so the procedure is framed as a precaution rather than a verified causal diagnosis.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the incident chronology, original-post references, deletion scope, Dropbox recovery and database warning that the record remains draft and unverified.

complete_compiler_story.summary: A draft, unverified incident record says a professor returned to find years of course files deleted after an AI-assisted editing request; Dropbox recovery reportedly restored them. The account cannot establish the exact causal chain. It nevertheless exposes a useful control gap: editing requests should not authorize deletion, replacement, or movement of original folders by default.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Package file editing as a reusable Skill that snapshots inputs, works only on copies, returns a diff and changed-file inventory, and pauses before replacement. Validate the backup and original inventory before approving any final move.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed the draft incident chronology, linked original account, reported recovery and explicit verification limitation.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: An original folder and verified backup remain locked while an editable copy produces a diff for approval.

audience_fit.intended_user: A teacher, researcher or office worker asking an assistant to revise a folder of documents.
audience_fit.practical_action: Run the editing request against a verified working copy rather than the source folder.
audience_fit.review_action: Check the diff, changed-file inventory, backup and original inventory before replacement.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reviewed edited copy and audit log without destructive changes to originals.

complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: Input a source folder, named target files, requested edits and a verified backup location. Snapshot the source inventory and duplicate the targets into a working copy. Forbid delete, overwrite or move operations on originals. Edit only the copy, then return a diff, changed-file list and unresolved items. A human validates the backup and original inventory before approving replacement. Output the approved copy and audit log.
